title: Conformance review
description: Departures from a stated rule registry on the five axes that require reading rather than matching. The registry this comes from carried eleven; four are a linter's under foundation/0004 R6, and two belong to other capabilities — security to security-scan and structure to architecture-scan — because one authoritative definition per concept means a rule has one home. Every finding cites a registry rule: a finding citing none is taste with a location attached, which is why `registry` is required at the top. `confidence` exists because a reviewer of an unfamiliar codebase produces contested findings, and marking them is what keeps the certain ones credible. No verdict: the source skill computed one from its own findings, which made the reviewer the gate.

review_id.description: Supplied by the caller and never minted by the producer.

reviewed.description: Every path reviewed. An empty findings array means nothing without it.

registry.description: The rule set reviewed against. Required: an absent registry is a stop for the producer rather than an invitation to supply its own rules.

findings.description: One entry per departure, sorted by file then line. Empty is a real result.

rule.description: The registry identifier. Exactly one per finding: a departure from two rules is two findings, because they are resolved separately.

axis.description: `contract_semantics` — code satisfying the letter of a declared interface and not its meaning — is the axis a linter cannot approach and the one that justifies the delegation.

evidence.description: The construct, quoted. For test_quality, the assertion itself.

cost.description: What goes wrong because of it, in terms of this code. A cost that reads as the rule's wording has no observation behind it.

confidence.description: `contested` where a reading of the rule could go either way; the alternative reading belongs in notes.
